content.title: About
content.content: A club sandwich is a multi‑layered sandwich typically made with toasted bread, chicken or turkey breast, ham, bacon, cheese, lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise. It is often cut into quarters and held together with a toothpick. The sandwich is a staple in restaurants and cafés worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first club sandwich appeared in the early 1920s at New York's "S. Club" restaurant.
The classic recipe uses three slices of bread, making it heartier than a regular sandwich.
In the United States the sandwich is called a "club" from "clubhouse", referring to dishes served in private clubs.
Variations include avocado, egg, tuna or vegetarian versions with grilled vegetables.
It is believed the original sandwich was created to use leftover meat and bread after dinner.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken, turkey and bacon provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain bread contain niacin, riboflavin and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Contains vegetables
items.content: Tomato and lettuce add vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole‑grain bread offers slow‑release glucose, helping maintain energy levels.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Bacon in moderation supplies monounsaturated fats, and olive‑oil‑based mayo adds omega‑9.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham, bacon and mayo can lead to excess salt intake, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Traditional bacon and mayo contain saturated fats that should be limited in heart‑related conditions.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise is often egg‑based and may trigger reactions in people with egg allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A club sandwich is calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is usually cut into four triangular pieces and secured with a toothpick. It can be eaten by hand, though a knife and fork are also acceptable. Additional sauces such as mustard or barbecue sauce can be added to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: If prepared ahead, keep the sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Separate the sauce and vegetables to prevent the bread from becoming soggy. Before serving, reheat the bacon and toast the bread to retain crispness.
